Ligand 1 is the acetyl probe; atom 17 is its cyclopropane CH bonded to the carbonyl at atom 15, the anchor that keeps the lightest cap. The aryl discovery reframes the rest of this run: a phenyl at the azine C4 gives jnk3 0.70 where every compact substituent capped at 0.61, so activity is no longer the constraint - lipophilicity is. Adding a benzene takes LogP past 5 and QED falls to 0.62, which is why that molecule scores worse than a bromine despite being far more active. The fix is to keep the ring and load it with nitrogen. A pyrimidin-5-yl is the most aggressive version: same flat six-membered ring in the same position, but two ring nitrogens instead of none, which is worth close to two log units and adds 26 of polar surface. If the activity is really about presenting a flat aromatic at that position rather than about its electron density - which is what the compact-substituent scan suggested, since donors and withdrawers scored alike - then this should hold near 0.70 with QED back in the 0.8s. Expected product: about 331 Da at LogP near 3.2.
